For generalized anxiety disorder, guided self-help and psychoeducation are usually the first-line treatments. If symptoms persist despite these interventions, high-intensity psychological therapy (CBT) or medication (SSRI antidepressants) is recommended. Both CBT and medication are considered equally effective in treating moderate to severe cases of generalized anxiety disorder [NICE Guideline CG113, 2019].

Alternative treatments such as fluoroquinolones should not be used without prior suitability assessment as they are typically reserved for certain resistant bacterial infections instead of being first-line agents for uncomplicated cystitis[IDsociety.org, 2019]. Please note, these citations are from the respective guidelines and fall under professional review rather than a diagnosis. 

Given the question specifically about generalized anxiety disorder treatment, focus on the guideline recommending CBT or an SSRI as the primary treatments following the initial intervention strategies.
